title: Cognitive Diagnostic Model Analysis of AI Safety Profiles

original_idea.body:
# Cognitive Diagnostic Model Analysis of AI Safety Profiles: Which Safety Attributes Does Each Model Master?

**Problem:** IRT produces a single ability score on a latent continuum. But safety is not a single ability — models may be able to refuse bioweapon requests but fail on subtle manipulation, or resist direct jailbreaks but fail on multi-step social engineering. Cognitive Diagnostic Models (CDMs), specifically the DINA or G-DINA model, produce a mastery profile (binary vector of skills mastered/not mastered) rather than a scalar score. This has never been applied to AI safety.

**Direction:** Step 1: Define a Q-matrix specifying which safety attributes (e.g., harmful content refusal, manipulation resistance, deception avoidance, bias mitigation) each benchmark item requires. This requires expert coding of 50-100 items from public benchmarks. Step 2: Fit a G-DINA model using the GDINA R package to safety benchmark response data. Step 3: Extract attribute mastery profiles for each AI model. Step 4: Cluster models by safety profile. Report which attributes are commonly mastered and which are systematically absent.

**Why it matters:** A CDM safety profile changes the question from 'how safe is this model?' to 'what exactly can and can't this model do safely?' This is far more actionable for AI developers and policymakers. It would be the first diagnostic safety profiling of AI models with formal psychometric foundations.

**Relevant context:** The GDINA R package is available and well-documented. CDM surveys (2024) confirm the technique is mature. LLM-CDM integration research (2025) shows the approach is feasible. Public safety benchmark item banks from TruthfulQA, BBQ, and HarmBench can provide response data.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: CDM produces mastery profiles revealing which specific safety attributes each model lacks, directly actionable for deployment decisions. Every link is explicit: Q-matrix -> G-DINA fit -> mastery profiles -> targeted safety remediation.

low_compute.reasoning: G-DINA model fitting in R (GDINA package) on existing data. CPU-only.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: CDM requires expert-level psychometric knowledge: designing Q-matrices, fitting G-DINA models, interpreting attribute mastery patterns. Advanced for even psychometrically-trained students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires expert coding of 50-100 items for Q-matrix before model fitting. Deliverable requires sustained effort across multiple steps.

quick_reasoning: Targets a specific, well-defined AI safety problem (diagnostic safety profiling revealing which safety attributes each model masters) with clear CDM methodology; safety relevance is obvious and the approach is novel.
